en_title: Building a Support Network Far From Home
en_excerpt: Far from home, expatriate mothers can rebuild the support network they miss — here are practical, accessible ways to start in Ireland.
en_meta_description: Practical ways for immigrant mothers in Ireland to build a support network, from parent and toddler groups to bilingual playgroups.
en_content:
Written by: Lili Fraga – Family & Children Intercultural & Emotional Development

Connections that strengthen immigrant wellbeing

Living outside your country of origin is, in itself, a dive into the unknown. But for expatriate mothers, the challenges multiply. Motherhood away from home carries layers of longing, tiredness, fear and, often, the temporary loss of your own identity. Who you were before you left seems distant — and now, as well as a mother, you are also an immigrant, starting from scratch in a place where you do not always speak the language or understand the social dynamics.

The absence of your support network — that grandmother, that friend, that neighbour — is sorely felt. The routine becomes heavier, rest becomes rarer, and self-esteem can begin to weaken. The good news? Even far from home, it is possible to build new networks. Perhaps different from the ones you knew, but just as powerful, genuine and welcoming.

Help does not always appear spontaneously, and that is okay. But know this: you can find or create spaces of support that hold you emotionally, help with the challenges of everyday life and remind you that you are not alone.

💡 Practical strategies for finding your network in Ireland

Here are some real, accessible ways to step out of isolation and start connecting with other people who share similar values:

👩‍👧‍👦 1. Groups for mothers and fathers (Parent & Toddler Groups)

Community spaces where mothers (or fathers) and their small children gather to play, socialise and swap experiences. Many are free or cost a token amount. 🔎 Where to find them: Family Resource Centres, local churches, crèches or community centres. E.g.: A Mother’s Embrace (Waterford), Barnardos, TUSLA parent support groups.

🤱 2. Bilingual or cultural playgroups

Taking part in groups that respect and celebrate your culture (such as groups of Brazilian or Latin American mothers) helps you feel seen and welcomed. 🔎 Look for groups on WhatsApp, Facebook (“Brasileiras na Irlanda”, “Mães em Dublin”, etc.), or in community schools.

☕ 3. Cafés for immigrants and themed in-person meet-ups

Moments designed to create connections: conversation circles, workshops, wellbeing and motherhood events. 🔎 Follow local projects such as Mum talks https://www.instagram.com/mum_talks/ 

🧘 4. Activities that combine self-care and company

Yoga classes, walking groups, art workshops or guided meditation with other mothers. A lovely way of looking after yourself while socialising. 🔎 Search Eventbrite, Meetup or Instagram for local activities using keywords such as “mothers”, “community wellness”, “creative circles”.

A few apps that can help you find the right group for you: – meetup.com– peanut-app.io– letsmush.com– nextdoor.ie

📱 5. Create your own network!

If you have not found anything that fits you, create it! A coffee at home with other mothers, a virtual support group and a picnic in the park. Someone is always waiting for that invitation.

💛 Wrapping up…

Connections heal. Belonging strengthens. Being seen transforms. Even far from your homeland, you can — little by little — rebuild your support network, surround yourself with people who welcome who you are today, and experience motherhood with more lightness and truth.

📌 And remember: seeking support is not selfishness. It is wisdom. You deserve to be well in order to care — including for yourself.
